paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the first bar, the lighter bar is 39.50%, and the darker bar is only 0.04%). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning on certain key principles eliminates bias to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across prompts specific to Support of Authorities and Extended Contact, also considerably reducing bias across Virtual Contact prompts.
model_annotation: The grouped and stacked bar chart illustrates the bias percentage across three distinct scenarios under varying contact conditions, both before and after an intervention. The horizontal category axis presents three groups in the following left-to-right order: Support of Authorities, Extended Contact, and Virtual Contact. The vertical value axis is labeled "Bias Percentage" and operates on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 70, with numeric tick marks spaced at regular intervals of 10. Within each of the three horizontal categories, bars are arranged in groups of three corresponding to different contact types, and each individual bar is stacked. According to the legend positioned below the chart, the bottom solid components represent the "Before" conditions, while the top hatched components represent the "After" conditions. Specifically, the leftmost stacked bar in each group consists of "No Contact Before" (solid light grey) and "No Contact After" (hatched dark grey); the middle bar consists of "Positive Contact Before" (solid light red) and "Positive Contact After" (hatched dark red); and the rightmost bar consists of "Negative Contact Before" (solid light blue) and "Negative Contact After" (hatched dark blue). Exact data values are annotated on the chart, with the "Before" values displayed inside the upper portion of the solid lower segments and the "After" values visually emphasized in bold text slightly above each bar. The solid "Before" segments range from a minimum value of 31.83 (Positive Contact Before under Support of Authorities) to a maximum of 47.28 (Negative Contact Before under Extended Contact). The hatched "After" segments are visually minimal or absent in the first two categories, showing values of 0.00, 0.04, and 0.11, whereas they are visibly taller in the Virtual Contact category, where they measure exactly 10.00, 10.01, and 10.02. The main categories are not sorted in a strictly alphabetical or ascending/descending order.
